P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: Gabriel John Utterson is a lawyer, the distant kinsman of Richard Enfield, and the friend and legal adviser of Dr. Jekyll. He is a man of steady habits, uneasy and concerned for Jekyll, and known as the last good influence on downgoing men. He introduced Enfield to Jekyll and long handled Jekyll's affairs, including a will naming Hyde as heir. When Poole came to him at night fearing foul play, Utterson followed him to Jekyll's house, questioned the servants, and resolved to break in. After the cabinet door was burst open, he found Hyde's body and searched for Jekyll. He now holds Jekyll's sealed packet and intends to read the documents and return before midnight to send for the police.

P10.tagline: Elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly butler of Dr. Jekyll's house and the servant who directs the search after the cabinet is broken open. He is frightened and worn, with a white face and a harsh broken voice, and for about a week he has been unable to bear the situation. He long served Jekyll, admitted Utterson to the cabinet, and reported that Jekyll confined himself over the laboratory. When he came to Utterson's house at night, he said the doctor had shut himself in and he feared foul play. He led Utterson to the laboratory, told of the masked figure, and struck the door with an axe. He now hands Utterson the sealed packet and awaits the police.

P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, owner of the house with laboratory and cabinet, and the friend and client of Mr. Utterson. He is tall and well built, known for charities and religion, but has become fanciful and estranged from Dr. Lanyon. His will left all his possessions to Edward Hyde, and he admitted Hyde dictated its terms. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, then resumed his old friendships before shutting his door against Utterson and vowing extreme seclusion. He was last seen sitting sadly at the middle window, declining to walk out. He is said to have been made away with eight days ago, and his body has not been found.

P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town, acquainted with Dr. Jekyll. He dislikes asking questions and calls this delicacy. He once collared a man who walked over a child and forced him to pay a hundred pounds, then spent the night in his chambers and proved the cheque genuine at the bank. He named the man as Hyde and described him as deformed and detestable. He later learned the sinister door was a back way to Jekyll's house. On a Sunday walk with Utterson he said the Hyde story was at an end, and after seeing Jekyll at the window he left the court in silence, pale with horror.

P20.tagline: Voice inside the cabinet refusing entry
P20.bio: The voice is the unseen speaker inside Dr. Jekyll's cabinet, heard by Poole and Mr. Utterson during the night search. It complains that it cannot see anyone and begs Utterson for mercy. It is connected to Poole only as the servant who knocks and calls through the door. After Poole reports that the doctor has shut himself in, the voice answers from within and refuses entry. Utterson recognizes it as Hyde's voice and orders the door down. The voice is now silent, its speaker found dead inside the cabinet.

P17.bio: The housemaid is a servant in Dr. Jekyll's house, subordinate to Poole and a colleague of the cook. She is hysterical and weeping. When Poole led Utterson into the hall, all the servants were huddled in fear, and she whimpered while the maid wept loudly. She remains in the hall with the other frightened servants as Utterson and Poole proceed to the laboratory. Her present situation is one of terror and grief among the household while the search for Jekyll continues.
